entries.name: small-tuple-const_one_item_type-v0-tx#0
entries.description: sigmaProp(c._1 == 1) where c is a CONSTANT of type `(Int)` — a one-item tuple TYPE, which the JVM parses and can never write back. At tree version 0, UNSIZED. THE CONTROL OF THIS PAIR, not evidence. The JVM refuses on the WRITE, after the parse succeeded; an implementation that refuses the tuple at PARSE has no degrade path at an unsized tree and refuses too. Both sides refuse for different reasons and the row grades GREEN. Its v3 twin is where the disagreement shows.

entries.name: small-tuple-const_one_item_type-v3-tx#1
entries.description: sigmaProp(c._1 == 1) where c is a CONSTANT of type `(Int)` — a one-item tuple TYPE, which the JVM parses and can never write back. At tree version 3, SIZE-FLAGGED. THE SEPARATING ROW. The JVM's answer is the same as at v0 — it parses the tree and then cannot write it back — but an implementation that refuses the tuple at PARSE now has the size bit to degrade behind: it stores the tree as opaque bytes and ACCEPTS the carrier the JVM rejects. An over-accept, and the only row of this pair that can show it.

entries.name: small-tuple-tuple_expr_128_items-v0-tx#10
entries.description: sigmaProp(Tuple(1 x 128)._1 == 1) — one past the boundary. The count byte 0x80 reads as -128 and `safeNewArray` bounds only the upper end, so the parse throws NegativeArraySizeException and takes the whole carrier with it. At tree version 0, UNSIZED. SEPARATING AT BOTH VERSIONS, and no degrade is involved: an implementation that reads the count UNSIGNED parses 128 items successfully and accepts the carrier. The JVM's refusal is a NegativeArraySizeException, which is not a ValidationException, so the size bit cannot turn it into a degrade either.

entries.name: small-tuple-register_one_item_type-tx#20
entries.description: R4 holds a CONSTANT of type `(Int)` — a one-item tuple type in a REGISTER rather than in the tree, on a box guarded by `sigmaProp(true)`. The box PARSES and the register reads back as `ConstantNode(Coll(1),(SInt$))`, a one-element `Coll[Any]` carrying a declared type of `(Int)`; writing it again throws in `w.putValue` (`ErgoBoxCandidate.scala:175`). ALSO A CONTROL: a register value sits outside the tree, so there is no size bit to degrade behind at any version and an implementation that refuses the tuple at parse refuses too. Green on both sides today; it is here to catch the over-accept if one ever starts reading such a type.

entries.name: small-tuple-register_nested_tuple_expr-tx#21
entries.description: R4 holds `Tuple(Tuple(1), 1)` — a pair whose FIRST item is a one-item tuple, as an EXPRESSION. `TupleSerializer` writes a count and no type, so the JVM writes this register itself and the carrier is valid. SEPARATING: an implementation whose tuples hold 2..255 refuses the nested one and so refuses a box the JVM accepts. The transaction tier carries its spend — `SELF.R4[((Int),Int)].isDefined` is true, and the value is `Coll(Coll(1),1)`, from which no field can be selected.
